rows.engine_path: _native.PyColumn.column(name) builds a DataFusion column-reference Expr directly.
rows.python_work: none semantic; sets spark_display/projection_name/stable_name/has_free_attribute and computes a structural sql_expr via _quote_column_sql_expr (double-quoted, per-segment for qualified names)
rows.notes: SQL_STRING side channel: sql_expr is a Python-built quoted identifier used by free-SQL surfaces (MERGE, global-agg select) — security-hardened per C3-SEC-001. Native path itself is clean.

rows.name: lit
rows.engine_path: Scalars → PyColumn.literal(value); date/datetime/time → PyColumn.sql("DATE '…'"/"TIMESTAMP '…'"/"TIME '…'"); list/tuple/ndarray → _scalar("array", *[lit(x) …]) with the ndarray form re-wrapped in PyColumn.sql(CAST(… AS ARRAY<T>)).
rows.python_work: branches on isinstance across enum.Enum (→.value), datetime.datetime (tz-normalize to UTC, strftime to text), datetime.date, datetime.time, numpy.ndarray, list/tuple, then scalar; rejects Column-in-list (COLUMN_IN_LIST) and unsupported types (PySparkTypeError); calls _coerce_lit_list_mixed_to_string to decide element coercion; builds display and SQL literal text via _lit_spark_display/_lit_sql_expr
rows.notes: SQL_STRING: the three temporal paths and the ndarray path are pure Python-built SQL text handed to PyColumn.sql — there is no native temporal/typed-array literal API, so those literals are engine-PARSED, not engine-CONSTRUCTED. Weakest ownership tier in this module after the partition transforms. Also: helper _coerce_lit_list_mixed_to_string does real value-level Python compute (str()/float() promotion, kind bucketing over elements) and _lit_numpy_ndarray does value.tolist()/.item() materialization — this is compute on user-supplied literal constants, not on rows, so it does not breach 'Python never touches rows', but it is the only value-computing code in the module besides abs. _lit_sql_expr special-cases NaN/±Inf to CAST('NaN' AS DOUBLE) forms (C6-SAF-002).

rows.name: expr
rows.engine_path: _native.PyColumn.sql(sql) — the engine parses the caller's SQL text into an Expr.
rows.python_work: only display cosmetics: strips the string and, if it is not already parenthesized and contains one of ' + ', ' - ', ' * ', ' / ', ' % ', wraps the display name in parens to match Spark's analyzer paren
rows.notes: Free-SQL escape hatch: the WHOLE expression is engine-parsed text, but Python builds none of it (user-supplied), so it is not SQL_STRING by the letter of the rule. Ownership-wise it is the same weak tier — no repark semantics are applied, and the docstring records a known gap: an expr() referencing a column raises (DataFrame-bound expr not implemented here).

rows.name: coalesce
rows.python_work: arity guard (raises AnalysisException on zero args); calls _reject_nested_generator on each arg; joins display/sql/join-sql fragments into 'coalesce(…)' f-strings; ORs sticky is_aggregate/has_free_attribute/has_ungroupable, ANDs is_foldable, carries partition_transform and H1 origin tokens
rows.notes: Three parallel spellings maintained by hand (spark_display, sql_expr, join_sql_expr) — SQL_STRING side channels, but all three are the same shape here so no divergence. Refusals are AnalysisException, not UnsupportedOperationException (zero-arg; UNSUPPORTED_GENERATOR for nested explode).

rows.name: concat
rows.engine_path: _native.PyColumn.concat([child exprs]) — Rust already wraps DataFusion concat in a CASE WHEN any-arg-IS-NULL guard plus a Utf8 cast for Spark null propagation.
rows.python_work: arity guard (AnalysisException); nested-generator refusal; hand-builds a SECOND null-propagation guard as SQL text — 'CASE WHEN (a IS NULL) OR … THEN CAST(NULL AS VARCHAR) ELSE concat(a, …) END'; ORs sticky aggregate/free-attr/ungroupable flags
rows.notes: DIVERGENCE PIN (SQL_STRING): Spark's any-null→NULL semantics are implemented TWICE — once in Rust (PyColumn::concat, Case + Cast to Utf8) and once again as Python-built SQL text for sql_expr. join_sql_expr is a THIRD spelling, a bare 'concat(…)' with NO null guard, so a join ON that embeds concat gets DataFusion skip-null semantics instead of Spark's. Any change to concat null semantics must touch all three sites.

rows.name: abs
rows.engine_path: No abs engine call at all: Python assembles lit(0) - column (PyColumn.literal + PyColumn.sub), column < 0 (PyColumn.lt), then when(...).otherwise(...) → Column._from_when_pairs → PyColumn.case_when.
rows.python_work: builds the negation as lit(0) - column, builds the predicate column < 0, wraps both in when(cond, negated).otherwise(column) to form a CASE, then OVERRIDES spark_display/projection_name/sql_expr/join_sql_expr to read 'abs(child)' regardless of the CASE plan shape; threads sticky aggregate/foldable/free-attr/ungroupable/partition_transform/origin from the child
rows.notes: MAJOR DIVERGENCE PIN: the native plan is a CASE expression while sql_expr/join_sql_expr claim 'abs(…)' — the two evaluation paths are different engine expressions with (only presumed) equal semantics; they differ for at least MIN_VALUE integer overflow and for any engine where abs() and the CASE disagree on type promotion. Docstring states it is deliberate ('no new Rust') so the compound aggregate name sum(abs(x)) pins bit-for-bit against the live PySpark oracle. Prime candidate for a real engine abs.

rows.name: count
rows.engine_path: Star path → PyColumn.count_aggregate([PyColumn.literal(1)], False); normal path → PyColumn.count_aggregate([child], False) → count_udaf().call(args).
rows.python_work: branches on the argument SHAPE: (a) isinstance(col, str) and col == '*' → builds count(1) over a literal 1 with sql_expr 'count(*)'; (b) isinstance(col, Column) whose _projection_name/_spark_display == '*' → recurses into count('*'); (c) otherwise coerces via _aggregate_argument and counts the child
rows.notes: Star detection is a Python STRING COMPARISON against a display/projection name — a Column whose display happens to be '*' is treated as count-all. Also a spelling divergence by design: native is count(Int64(1)) while sql_expr is 'count(*)' (comment explicitly forbids fixing it by substring replace — octo C2-SAF-001). The star branch returns without threading origin tokens.

rows.name: count_distinct
rows.engine_path: PyColumn.count_aggregate(natives, True) → count_udaf().call(count_distinct_argument(args)).distinct() — Rust packs multi-arg into a null-if-any struct.
rows.python_work: coerces every arg through _aggregate_argument; branches on len(columns) == 1 vs > 1 to choose the SQL text: single → 'count(DISTINCT a)'; multi → hand-built 'count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (a IS NOT NULL) AND … THEN struct(a, b) END)'; builds agg_name 'count(DISTINCT a, b)'
rows.notes: DIVERGENCE PIN (SQL_STRING): the null-if-any struct packing that gives Spark's 'exclude the row if ANY column is NULL' semantics exists TWICE — in Rust (count_distinct_argument) and re-spelled as Python SQL text for the free-SQL path. join_sql_expr is a THIRD spelling, plain 'count(DISTINCT a, b)', which DataFusion rejects for multi-arg — latent failure if a join ON ever embeds a multi-column count_distinct.

Also normalizes returnType to a logical simpleString DDL and functionType to an int eval-type tag.
rows.notes: SANCTIONED EXCEPTION (per audit brief): the user-supplied Python body executes over real row data at action time (vectorized Series-per-batch), so the 'Python never touches rows' rule is deliberately waived here. DIVERGENCE PINS: window form is GROUPED_AGG + .over only; functionType='WINDOW' is a hard refuse. This whole module makes ZERO engine calls — no _scalar, no call_scalar, no PyColumn construction; the only engine touch anywhere is col(name) for str arguments in the two __call__ methods.

NULL-propagation parity is therefore Python-owned, not engine-owned — a divergence risk if the engine ever grows a native array_append.

Plan-building only — no rows touched — but a prime candidate for a native kernel.
